implementation_notes: The framework already owns every role: RequestDelegate is the interceptor callback, the middleware pipeline is the dispatcher, HttpContext is the context, and app.Use(...) registers while app.Run(...) terminates deliberately. The class-based form is IMiddleware (invoke(HttpContext, RequestDelegate next)) when the middleware needs constructor injection; the classic Interceptor/Dispatcher class pair is replaced by delegate composition, so hand-rolling a registry on top adds nothing. For interception at the object level instead of the request level (transactions, caching on a service interface), use System.Reflection.DispatchProxy or Castle DynamicProxy - the two mechanisms are complementary, not alternatives to the same job.
pitfalls: Order is the contract: a Use registered after a Run (terminal) delegate never executes, and short-circuiting middleware silently hides everything registered later - the docs show a never-reached Use for exactly this reason.
Writing headers or a status code after next() has started the response throws (check context.Response.HasStarted); a 'post-processing' middleware must only decorate a response that is still buffered.

Middleware registered with app.Use is a singleton for the app's lifetime: injecting scoped services through the constructor creates a captive dependency - take them as InvokeAsync parameters or implement IMiddleware.

variants.name: DispatchProxy object interception on an interface
variants.implementation_notes: Object-scoped interception from the base class library: a DispatchProxy subclass receives every call on the proxied interface as MethodInfo plus arguments, so cross-cutting work (timing, authorization, caching, retry) runs around the target without the caller changing. Attachment is per instance (create the proxy instead of the concrete object), which makes it easy to add and remove at run time but means interception only exists where the proxy was inserted - unlike the request pipeline, which covers every call by construction. Castle DynamicProxy is the richer third-party option when class proxying, async-aware hooks or method filtering are needed.
pitfalls: Interfaces only: DispatchProxy cannot proxy virtual members of a class - reaching for it on a sealed/internal or class-based service fails, which is where Castle DynamicProxy is needed.
Reflection invocation wraps target exceptions in TargetInvocationException, changing the exception contract callers see; unwrap the inner exception explicitly.
Each proxy instance has its own interceptor instance, so shared state (counters, caches) must be static/thread-safe or injected, and the proxy must never be cast back to the concrete type.
